clue.text: This is it!

parts.note: the puzzle ran on America's national holiday, so 'this' points to the very date of publication

explanation.walkthrough: The clue only works with the paper in hand: it appeared on 4 July, and 'this' is the day you are reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was printed on America's Independence Day, so the date is literally the day in question.

clue.text: Problem of space was reported to this US city

definitions.text: Problem of space was reported to this US city

parts.words: Problem of space was reported to this US city
parts.note: recalls the Apollo 13 crew radioing mission control in Texas with the famous words 'we have a problem'

explanation.surface: A trouble in outer space is relayed to an American city's control centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem of space' sounds like a shortage of room, but it is a malfunction in outer space on the Apollo 13 mission.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA's Mission Control is in this Texas city, which received the famous Apollo 13 distress call.

clue.text: This could be the start of something big

definitions.text: This could be the start of something big

parts.words: This could be the start of something big
parts.note: the stone laid ceremonially when a large building is begun

explanation.surface: An encouraging remark about a promising beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like optimism about a venture; literally it is the first block laid for a big building.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a block is laid ceremonially to mark the beginning of construction of a large building.

clue.text: Like territory nobody has taken steps to explore

definitions.text: Like territory nobody has taken steps to explore

parts.words: Like territory nobody has taken steps to explore
parts.note: 'taken steps' is read literally as walking: ground no foot has crossed

explanation.surface: Describing land that nobody has yet made any effort to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken steps' usually means made arrangements; here it means literally walked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground never walked upon is unvisited and unexplored by foot.

clue.text: Large US company, we hear, secured by bonds

indicators.note: the hearers are told the letters are spelt as a sound-alike of the company word

parts.note: a trust is a big American business combine, as in antitrust law

explanation.surface: A big American firm, it is said, is backed by financial bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonds' suggests finance but means ropes or ties. In American usage a trust is a large commercial combine.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tied up with ropes or cords is to be bound tightly.

clue.text: American award that can give actors no end of excitement

indicators.note: the word actors is able to yield the answer when its letters are rearranged
signals that a letter must be left out of the word actors
takes the final letter of the word excitement

explanation.surface: A Hollywood prize that thrills performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of excitement' removes T, the last letter of 'excitement', from ACTORS, leaving ACORS, which 'can give' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is popularly known by this nickname.

clue.text: Whence one starts out for remote area in US

definitions.meaning: a point of departure for a journey or venture
in American usage, a far-off outpost at the edge of civilisation

explanation.surface: A place to begin a journey into the American back country.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a starting point and, in American English, an out-of-the-way spot.

clue.text: President shot in dramatic circumstances

parts.note: 'dramatic' is literal: the assassination took place in a theatre

explanation.surface: A head of state is gunned down in sensational fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic' seems to mean sensational, but the killing happened at Ford's Theatre in Washington in 1865.
explanation.definitionFit: This sixteenth US president was assassinated at a play in Ford's Theatre.

clue.text: Splendid month in city in Georgia cut short

definitions.meaning: the eighth month of the year

explanation.surface: A fine month spent in a Georgia city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue adds a third route: AUGUSTA, the city in Georgia, 'cut short' by losing its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stately and grand, and it is also the summer month after July.

clue.text: Top-class computer replacing original two in Wyoming soon

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters of the state name is swapped out for another piece

explanation.surface: A first-rate computer is coming soon to a Wyoming office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacing original two in' swaps WY, the first two letters of WYOMING, for PC, giving PCOMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming up is forthcoming, about to happen shortly.

clue.text: Hard-working filmmaker associated with America

explanation.surface: A diligent movie company with American links.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent person devoted to reading and learning is bookish and industrious.

clue.text: Republican greeting numbers here for big game

explanation.surface: A Republican politician greets the crowds who have gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' means large animals hunted on safari, not a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: These large horned African animals are classic quarry of safari hunters.

clue.text: Land of the free, one declares

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Land of the free, one declares (6)' defines and builds the linked answer UNITED STATES (one = UNITED, declares = STATES) over 13 and 25, but the puzzle file records no group, so the wordplay cannot be filed for UNITED alone
annotationWithheld.clue: Land of the free, one declares

clue.text: Hoover, for example, getting old and harmful

parts.note: the Hoover Dam is on the Colorado River

explanation.surface: A vacuum cleaner that is wearing out and causing harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoover' suggests a vacuum cleaner, but it is the Hoover Dam on the Arizona-Nevada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Something injurious causes harm or hurt.

clue.text: Serious offence creating violent storm in L.A.

indicators.note: a violent upheaval throws the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A grave crime produces a ferocious storm in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave sin cuts the soul off from grace.

clue.text: People like Annie Oakley taking drug to mid-West

indicators.note: takes the central letters of the word West

explanation.surface: Wild West women take narcotics to the Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie Oakley was a celebrated American sharpshooter of the Wild West shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Admired women of courage or fame are examples of the female hero.

clue.text: Oddly, mere boy is eminent American poet

indicators.note: done oddly, the four letters of mere come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Strangely, a mere lad becomes a celebrated poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' rearranges MERE as EMER. 'Oddly' tempts you to take odd letters, but that gives too few.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a leading nineteenth-century American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Declared independence in some English colonies, originally — revolutionary deed

indicators.note: taking the opening letter of each of the three words
a revolution turns the letters of deed over into a new order

explanation.surface: American colonies broke away from England in a revolutionary act.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw formally from a union is to break away and become separate.

clue.text: From Rhode Island, individual personality returned weapons

indicators.note: the word for individual personality is read backwards

parts.note: your self is your individual identity

explanation.surface: A character from Rhode Island sent back the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-barrelled guns fired from the shoulder are arms.

clue.text: Far-out values taken out of context, remarkably

indicators.note: the letters are lifted straight from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Extreme figures quoted out of context, strikingly.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics these are maximum and minimum points of a function.

clue.text: A lot of high-fliers in Boeing, for example

parts.note: a set is a group or lot

explanation.surface: Many wealthy travellers flying in a Boeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable wealthy people who travel widely form a glamorous elite.

clue.text: E.g., Oklahoma, in musical terms? Right

definitions.meaning: Oklahoma! is the name of a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical
a legal entitlement, as to property

explanation.surface: Oklahoma's name in a musical is a matter of right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the name of a work and a legal claim to ownership.

clue.text: Capitol's reconstructed as feature of West Virginia

indicators.note: the letters are built up again in a new order

explanation.surface: The Capitol is rebuilt as a landmark of West Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Capitol's' counts as a letter here. West Virginia is famous for its mining.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal mines are a characteristic part of West Virginia's landscape and economy.

clue.text: Guided round Colorado, in wild desert

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the state abbreviation
something wild is uncontrolled, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A guide led travellers round Colorado through untamed desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles the desert's letters and 'round' wraps them about the state's abbreviation; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead or accompany someone is to conduct them.

clue.text: See 13

annotationWithheld.why: 'See 13': second light of the linked answer UNITED STATES, which the puzzle file holds with no group, so its wordplay sits in clue 13

clue.text: City in 13+25

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'City in 13+25 (12,3)', gives only INDEPENDENCE (a city in the United States); nothing supplies DAY, so the clue looks cut short in OCR
